numeric_values_checked.description:
Finite numeric values examined across all columns. 0 means the
dimension had nothing to assess and it is excluded from the overall
score.

ColumnProfile.description: Profiling statistics for a single column.

invalid_count.description:
Non-null values that failed the column type's raw validity predicate:
non-finite or malformed numbers on numeric columns, and values that do
not parse directly as calendar dates on date columns. The date predicate
intentionally does not trim surrounding whitespace; descriptive date
statistics may normalize whitespace independently.

For numeric columns, `mean`/`std_dev` cover
`total_count - null_count - invalid_count` values. For date columns,
this count audits the strict raw-value quality predicate. `None` means
the check did not run (another column type, or statistics skipped) —
never "no invalid values", which is `Some(0)`.

patterns.description:
Detected patterns, or `None` when pattern detection did not run.

`None` and `Some(vec![])` are not interchangeable: the former means the
column was never scanned, the latter that it was scanned and nothing
matched. Consumers that gate on sensitivity -- redaction, agent-facing
output -- must treat `None` as "unknown", never as "no sensitive data".

type_homogeneity.description:
How the column's non-null values distribute across lexical classes.

`data_type` cannot answer "did this column have a dominant form?": a
column of names and a column that is 60% numbers are both `String`, and
`invalid_count` is absent on string columns by contract. This carries the
evidence, so a consumer can tell a textual column from one that defeated
type inference.

Counted over the values the profiler retained — the engine's bounded
reservoir sample on a large source, the whole column on a small or
in-memory one. `classified_count()` against `total_count - null_count`
is what says which happened; treat the shares as sampled whenever it is
short.

`None` means the classification did not run, never "one uniform class":
a column that was classified and had nothing to classify (all-null, or
zero rows) is `Some` with every count zero.

unique_count_is_approximate.description:
Whether `unique_count` is an approximate (HyperLogLog) estimate rather
than an exact distinct count.

`None` when `unique_count` is `None` (never computed); `Some(false)` for
an exact count; `Some(true)` once the cardinality estimator has spilled
to its HLL sketch (~1% relative error). Consumers running key or
high-cardinality/uniqueness gates must treat `Some(true)` as "do not rely
on this as an exact integer" -- an exact-looking count with no provenance
is unsafe for those checks.

ColumnStats.description: Type-specific statistics for a column, determined by the inferred data type.

complete_records_ratio.description:
Percentage of records in which every field is present, counted over
every row the engine read. Strict by design: a record missing one
optional field is not complete, so read it beside `null_columns`,
which names the columns responsible.

total_cells.description:
Total cells examined (rows × columns). 0 means the dimension had
nothing to assess and it is excluded from the overall score.

values_checked.description:
Non-null values examined for type consistency. 0 means the dimension
had nothing to assess and it is excluded from the overall score.

DataFrameLibrary.description: Source library for in-memory DataFrame profiling

oneOf.description: File-based data source (CSV, JSON, Parquet, etc.)

parquet_metadata.description: Parquet-specific metadata (only present for Parquet files)

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the file

engine.description: Database engine used for the query

row_count.description: Number of rows at profiling time

oneOf.description:
In-memory byte buffer profiled without a path behind it. The buffer may
be text (CSV/JSON/JSONL) or binary (Parquet); `format` says which.
Distinguished from [`DataSource::DataFrame`]: the caller handed over
bytes, not a schema-bearing dataframe, so provenance must say so.

format.description: Format the buffer was parsed as

size_bytes.description: Length of the buffer handed over, not of the values decoded from it

batch_id.description: Batch identifier for ordering and deduplication

first_record_at.description: Timestamp of first record in batch (ISO 8601)

last_record_at.description: Timestamp of last record in batch (ISO 8601)

source_system.description: Source system identifier (kafka, kinesis, pulsar, http, etc.)

topic.description: Stream identifier (e.g., Kafka topic, Kinesis stream name)

oneOf.description: Identifier values that should be treated as semantic strings.
Whole numbers in the i64 range.

bytes_consumed.description: Number of bytes consumed from the source, if known.

columns_detected.description: Number of columns detected in the data.

engine.description: Engine or parser that actually produced the report.

error_count.description: Number of errors encountered during profiling.

memory_peak_mb.description:
Peak process memory usage (resident set size) in megabytes observed
during profiling, sampled at chunk/batch boundaries. Absent when the
platform provided no reading or the input path does not track memory.

ragged_row_count.description:
Number of data rows whose field count differed from the header's.

These rows were recovered — extra trailing fields dropped, missing
trailing fields padded to null — so profiling continued, but each one
is a structural violation in the source. A nonzero value means the file
did not parse cleanly even though a report was produced. Additive field:
legacy documents without it deserialize as `0`.

rows_processed.description: Number of rows actually processed or analyzed.

sampling_ratio.description: Ratio of rows analyzed to total rows when sampling is meaningful.

source_exhausted.description: Whether the entire source was consumed.

throughput_rows_sec.description: Throughput in rows per second, auto-calculated when possible.

truncation_reason.description: If the source was not exhausted, why processing stopped.

FileFormat.description: Supported file formats for data profiling

FrequencyItem.description: A value and its frequency count within a column.

oneOf.description:
No dimension had anything to assess, so there is no score for the
other variants to describe. Reporting `Exact` here would claim
certainty about a number that was never computed.

NumericStats.description: Statistics for numeric (integer or float) columns.

outlier_count.description:
Number of values flagged as IQR-based outliers in this column.

Uses the same Tukey-style detection (Q1 − k·IQR, Q3 + k·IQR with
k = 1.5 by default) that feeds the global `accuracy.outlier_ratio`.
`None` when outlier detection didn't run (sample below the configured
minimum or non-numeric column).

num_row_groups.description: Number of row groups in the Parquet file

Pattern.description: A detected value pattern within a column (e.g. email, phone, UUID).

confidence.description: Detection confidence score (0.0--1.0), derived from pattern specificity and match rate

match_count.description: Number of values matching this pattern

PatternCategory.description: Semantic category for a detected pattern.

PrecisionMetrics.description: Precision metrics for effective decimal-scale consistency.

numeric_values_checked.description: Parseable finite values examined in floating-point columns.

ProfileReport.description:
Complete profiling report for a data source.

Contains column-level statistics, execution metadata, and an optional
Quality assessment informed by ISO 8000/25012 concepts. This is the primary output of all
profiling operations (`Profiler::analyze_file`, `Profiler::analyze_source`,
`Profiler::profile_stream`, etc.).

execution.description: Execution metadata (timing, rows processed, truncation info, etc.)

id.description: Unique identifier for this report (UUID v4)

quality.description: Data quality assessment (optional — partial analysis may skip quality)

schema_version.description:
Version of the serialized report schema (see [`REPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION`]).

`0` means the document predates schema versioning (a 0.9-era report).
Deserialization rejects versions newer than [`REPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION`].

semantic_hint_bindings.description:
Per-column evidence of how each semantic hint bound to the data.

Empty when no hints were supplied. Recorded for provenance: a hint proven
inert over the full data is rejected before a report is returned, so a
successful report only carries bindings that matched something or whose
evidence was sampled. Additive field — older readers ignore it.

timestamp.description: Timestamp when the report was generated (ISO 8601 / RFC 3339)

type_homogeneity.description:
Counts per lexical class. The Python dialect writes them as a plain
mapping, but it is the same four-key object the Rust dialect writes, so
it is described by the same definition: a reader that accepted a partial
mapping here would validate a document the Python loader then discards
as incomplete rather than inventing the missing counts.

avg_length.description: Mean length, in Unicode scalar values. See `min_length`.

max_length.description: Longest value, in Unicode scalar values. See `min_length`.

min_length.description:
Shortest value, in Unicode scalar values. Not UTF-8 bytes and not
grapheme clusters: ASCII text is unaffected by that distinction, while a
combining sequence counts each scalar, so the decomposed and precomposed
spellings of the same word report different lengths.

overall_score.description:
Null when no dimension was assessable; `assessed_dimensions` is then
empty and every entry in `dimension_scores` is null.

QualityAssessment.description: Wraps quality metrics with confidence information.

QualityMetrics.description: Comprehensive data quality metrics following industry standards.

low_sample_warning.description:
True when the sample used to compute these metrics was below the
minimum recommended size (10 rows). When set, the quality scores and
per-dimension ratios should be treated as directional rather than
reliable. Backwards-compatible: defaults to `false`.

score_weights.description:
Weights used to aggregate dimension scores. Default weights are omitted
from serialized reports; custom weights are retained for reproducible
score calculation after a round trip.

QualityScoreWeights.description:
Relative weights used to aggregate assessed quality dimensions.

Weights do not need to sum to one: the score renormalizes them over the
dimensions that were actually assessed. Values should be non-negative and
at least one weight must be positive.

QueryEngine.description: Supported query engines for SQL-based profiling

SemanticHintBinding.description:
Per-column evidence of whether a semantic hint actually bound to any value.

A hint expresses user domain knowledge about a column; this records how much
of the column that knowledge matched. `matched_values` counts the values of
the kind the hint expects (numeric for `positive`, date-parseable for
`temporal`, every non-null value for `identifier`, which coerces the column).

`exact` distinguishes a full-data count from a sampled one: a hint that
matched nothing (`matched_values == 0`) is only *proven* inert when the count
covers every row. A sampled zero is recorded but never treated as an error,
because absence in a sample is not proof of absence in the data.

column.description: The hinted column this evidence is for.

exact.description: Whether the counts cover every row (`true`) or a sample (`false`).

kind.description: Which hint list named the column.

matched_values.description: Values that matched the hint's expected kind.

SemanticHintKind.description: The kind of a semantic hint, used for diagnostics and binding evidence.

TextStats.description:
Statistics for text/string columns.

Every length here is a count of Unicode scalar values, not UTF-8 bytes and
not grapheme clusters. ASCII text is unaffected by that distinction; a
combining sequence counts each scalar, so the decomposed and precomposed
spellings of the same word report different lengths. The `text_units` module
carries the reasoning.

avg_length.description:
Mean length in Unicode scalar values. A mean, so it rounds at the
statistics precision rather than the percentage one.

max_length.description: Longest value, in Unicode scalar values.

min_length.description: Shortest value, in Unicode scalar values.

date_values_checked.description:
Non-null values examined in inferred or explicitly configured temporal
columns. 0 means
the dimension had nothing to assess and it is excluded from the
overall score.

invalid_date_values.description:
Non-null values in inferred or explicitly configured temporal columns
that failed calendar-date parsing.

temporal_pairs_checked.description:
Start/end value pairs actually compared for temporal ordering.
`temporal_violations` is bounded by this, not by
`date_values_checked` — the pair scan may cover columns the date
scan does not.

TruncationReason.description: Reason why profiling was truncated before exhausting the source.

oneOf.description: Stopped after processing a maximum number of rows.
Stopped after consuming a maximum number of bytes.
Stopped due to a user-defined stop condition.
The input stream was closed by the producer.

TypeHomogeneity.description:
How a column's non-null values distribute across [`LexicalClass`]es.

Raw counts rather than a share, so that a reader can state the mixture it
actually found ("60% numeric, 40% text") instead of the dominant class and
an unnamed remainder, and so a serialized report carries no rounded
derivative of a number it does not also carry exactly.

All four counts are always present. Every field zero means the column was
classified and had no non-null values to classify — "analyzed, found
nothing", which is not the same as an absent `type_homogeneity`.

duplicate_rows_approximate.description:
True when `duplicate_rows` comes from the full-stream distinct-count
estimator after it spilled to its HLL sketch (~1% relative error on
the distinct count), rather than an exact count.

key_column.description:
Column whose uniqueness `key_uniqueness` describes. `None` means no
key column was identified; `key_uniqueness` then carries no signal
and does not contribute to the dimension score.

rows_checked.description:
Rows scanned for exact duplicates. 0 means the dimension had nothing
to assess and it is excluded from the overall score.

ValidityMetrics.description: Validity metrics derived from confidently detected semantic patterns.

values_checked.description: Non-null values checked against a dominant semantic pattern.

description:
Both v1 serialization dialects accepted by dataprof.

Rust serializes the complete runtime model. The high-level Python wrapper
predates that shape and exposes a deliberately flatter document. They share
one schema version and compatibility policy, so the published artifact
describes their union rather than pretending one dialect does not exist.
